cohort: The study included 19 mother-infant dyads, consisting of 6 pregnant women with opioid use disorder treated with naltrexone and their infants, compared with 13 treated with buprenorphine and their infants.
finding: Maintaining pregnant women on naltrexone was associated with significantly lower rates of neonatal abstinence syndrome (NAS) diagnosis, pharmacologic treatment for NAS, and shorter infant hospital length of stay compared to buprenorphine.
